key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically extract key longitudinal breast oncology variables from dense narrative charts with high agreement to expert abstraction.
clinical_relevance: This could substantially reduce the time and labor needed to build research datasets from real-world oncology records, especially for outcomes and biomarkers often buried in notes.
method: Randomly sampled 100 breast cancer patients from an institutional cohort.
Compared four general-purpose LLMs against oncologist abstraction, genetic testing records, and some coordinator-abstracted variables.
Used an open-source, HIPAA-compliant pipeline without fine-tuning or hand-selecting input documents.
evidence_signal: In the main cohort, the best models (GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro) reached 90%-100% concordance for several key variables, and in a separate 97-patient cohort the same pipeline showed similar recurrence-detection performance.
watch_item: Performance was weaker for therapy-line reconstruction than for simpler variable extraction, so external validation and institution-specific testing are still needed before broad deployment.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
